presentation_summary: 21-year-old man with remote splenectomy at age 16 presented with 3 weeks of intermittent fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.
He was febrile to 38.4 C on presentation; chest X-ray was interpreted as left lower lobe pneumonia and CT abdomen showed only post-surgical changes after splenectomy.
Laboratory evaluation showed marked leukocytosis averaging 30,000-68,000/uL and peaking at 81,000/uL, with peripheral smear showing absolute lymphocytosis and atypical lymphocytes.
Broad-spectrum antibiotics for 5 days did not resolve fever; flow cytometry showed marked T-cell expansion suggestive of viral infection.
CMV IgM was 110 U/mL, CMV IgG 1.40 U/mL, and CMV DNA 68,265 copies/mL; ganciclovir started on hospital day 9 with fever resolution within 48 hours.
